chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Al-Abbas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Sa’dan ibn Muslim - whose name was Abdul Rahman ibn Muslim, on the authority of al-Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abi Ja’far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ten [characteristics] by which one meets God, the Mighty and Majestic, shall enter Paradise: bearing witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family); confessing to what came from God, the Mighty and Majestic; establishing prayer; giving alms-tax; fasting in the month of Ramadan; pilgrimage to the House; accepting the Guardianship of the Divine Leaders; and condemning God’s enemies; and avoiding all intoxicating drinks.

key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting in the month of Ramadan (Sawm)

ai.seo_question: What are the ten characteristics required to enter Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) synthesizes the outward pillars of Islam with the inward dimensions of Shia theology, specifically highlighting Wilayah and Bara'ah as essential criteria for divine acceptance. This enumeration reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inseparability of creed (Aqidah), worship (Ibadah), and ethical conduct (Akhlaq) in achieving salvation. The inclusion of 'confession to what came from God' underscores the comprehensive acceptance of divine revelation, while avoiding intoxicants signifies the preservation of spiritual clarity.
